filters.name: Measure Topological Properties
filters.shortDescription: Compute a set of topological measures over a mesh or a polyline.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Compute a set of topological measures over a mesh: vertex, edge and face counts, connected components, manifoldness, holes and genus, and the faces that are duplicated (same three vertices), have zero area or are degenerate (repeat a vertex; they are zero-area too). It also tells whether the faces are consistently oriented, which is only defined when no edge is non-manifold: with such edges the `is_mesh_oriented` output is absent.

For a **polyline** (the real edges of a layer, as made by the *Create Polyline* filters) it reports instead its connected pieces; its **ends** (vertices with one edge) and **junctions** (three or more); the **strands**, the chains running between ends and junctions, a closed loop with neither counting as one strand; the closed loops; and the independent cycles, $E - V + C$. A tree has none; the cut graph of a closed surface of genus $g$ has $2g$. A layer with both faces and edges gets both reports. A point cloud has no topology to measure.

filters.name: Measure Topological Properties for Quad Mesh
filters.shortDescription: Compute a set of topological measures over a quad mesh.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Compute a set of topological measures over a quad mesh.

filters.name: Measure Geometric Properties
filters.shortDescription: Compute a set of geometric measures of a mesh, point cloud or polyline.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Compute a set of geometric measures of a mesh/pointcloud. Bounding box extents and diagonal, principal axis, thin shell barycenter (mesh only), vertex barycenter and quality-weighted barycenter (pointcloud only), surface area and boundary length (mesh only), the same two scaled so that the longest side of the bounding box is 1 (`normalized_surface_area`, `normalized_boundary_length`, which makes meshes of different size comparable), volume (closed mesh) and inertia tensor matrix (closed mesh).

For a **polyline** (the real edges of a layer) it reports the total length, the shortest, longest and average edge, and the barycenter and principal axes of the wire, every point of every edge weighing alike, so a densely sampled stretch does not pull them towards itself. A layer with both faces and edges gets both. Measures are taken in world space, through the layer matrix.

filters.name: Measure UV Mapping
filters.shortDescription: Report the UV islands, folds and quasi-conformal distortion of a UV mapping, in texels.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Reports how the texture coordinates of the current layer lay its surface out, with the measures of the TexMetro tool behind the *Real-World Textured Things* benchmark (the output keys are its own). Both per-wedge and per-vertex coordinates are measured.

UV coordinates are taken **in texels**: those of each face are scaled by the size of its texture image, so the stretch of a non-square texture counts, or by the size given in *Texture Width* and *Texture Height*. A layer with no texture image and no size is measured in its own unit square, and says so. Measures are taken in world space, through the layer matrix.

- **UV islands** (`num_charts`, what TexMetro calls charts): the maximal sets of faces connected across edges whose UV agree on both sides. `num_null_charts` counts those with no UV area. `en_uv` and `en_uv_b` are the edges of the layout and those on its boundary, where a seam is two edges, one for each side; `area_uv` and `boundary_len_uv` are its area and boundary length, in texels.

- **Folds** (`nfolds`): the faces whose UV orientation is opposite to that of their island. A face with no UV area is not a fold. (TexMetro counts it as one when the sign of its zero differs from the island's.)

- **Mapped fraction** (`mapped_fraction`): the share of the surface whose faces have both surface area and UV area.

- **Quasi-conformal distortion** (`qcd_*`): the ratio between the largest and the smallest stretch of the map from a face to its UV triangle,

$$Q=\frac{\sigma_{\max}}{\sigma_{\min}},$$

which is $1$ for a map that preserves angles whatever its scale. It does not see orientation, so a fold counts as its mirror image. Percentiles (`qcd_perc1` to `qcd_perc99`), minimum, maximum, mean, root mean square, variance and standard deviation are weighted by the surface area of each face. Faces with $Q$ at or above the threshold are outliers: they are left out, and their area is reported in `qcd_discardedArea`. Faces with no surface or UV area, and infinite values, are not counted at all.

- **Occupancy** (`occupancy`): the share of the texels that hold a triangle, once the overwritten ones are counted once. It needs the texture size, as does the next measure; without it they are left out.

- **UV scaling** (`sf_*`): the area of a face in the layout over its area on the surface, divided by the same ratio for the whole mesh, so $1$ is the texel density of the mesh as a whole. Its percentiles and moments are weighted by surface area like the distortion's, and a face whose UV area is more than the threshold times its share of the texels the layout really uses (occupancy times the texture area) is an outlier, reported in `sf_discardedArea`. The texels are counted as *Measure Texel Coverage* does.

parameters.label: Texture Width
parameters.help: Width in texels in which to measure the UV, for every texture. With 0 each face takes the width of its own texture image, and a layer with no image is measured in its unit square. Set Texture Height with it.

parameters.label: Texture Height
parameters.help: Height in texels in which to measure the UV, for every texture. With 0 each face takes the height of its own texture image. Set Texture Width with it.

parameters.label: UV Scaling Threshold
parameters.help: A face is an outlier of the UV scaling when its UV area is more than this many times its share of the texels the layout covers: it is left out of the statistics and its area is reported apart. TexMetro uses 100.

parameters.label: Subpixel Bits
parameters.help: Bits of position inside a texel to which the triangles' vertices are rounded when texels are counted, as a GPU rasterizer does: 4 is the least OpenGL guarantees, 8 the usual hardware. It changes the rare counts by up to about one percent.

parameters.label: Distortion Threshold
parameters.help: Faces whose quasi-conformal distortion is at or above this value are outliers: they are left out of its statistics and their area is reported apart. TexMetro uses 100.

filters.name: Measure Texel Coverage
filters.shortDescription: Count how the UV triangles cover the texels of each texture, at each mipmap level.

parameters.label: Texture Width
parameters.help: Width in texels in which to count, for every texture. With 0 each texture takes the width of its own image. Set Texture Height with it.

parameters.label: Texture Height
parameters.help: Height in texels in which to count, for every texture. With 0 each texture takes the height of its own image. Set Texture Width with it.

parameters.label: Mip Levels
parameters.help: Count the texture itself and every mipmap level below it, or the texture itself only.

parameters.label: Subpixel Bits
parameters.help: Bits of position inside a texel to which the triangles' vertices are rounded: 4 is the least OpenGL guarantees, 8 the usual hardware. It changes the rare counts by up to about one percent.

parameters.label: Clash Neighbours
parameters.help: Which neighbours of a texel are compared for a clash with another UV island: the four diagonal ones, as TexMetro does, or all eight.

filters.name: Measure Selection Area and Perimeter
filters.shortDescription: Compute area and perimeter of the face selection.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Compute area and perimeter of the FACE selection.

filters.name: Measure Vertex Scalar Statistics
filters.shortDescription: Compute aggregate statistics over per-vertex quality.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Compute some aggregate statistics over the per vertex quality, like Min, Max, Average, StdDev and Variance.

filters.name: Measure Face Scalar Statistics
filters.shortDescription: Compute aggregate statistics over per-face quality.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Compute some aggregate statistics over the per face quality, like Min, Max, Average, StdDev and Variance.

filters.name: Measure Vertex Scalar Histogram
filters.shortDescription: Compute a histogram of per-vertex quality values.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Compute an histogram of the values of the per-vertex quality. It can be useful to evaluate the distribution of the quality value over the surface. It can be discrete (e.g. based on vertex count or area weighted).

parameters.label: Hist Min
parameters.help: Lower bound of the histogram range.

parameters.label: Hist Max
parameters.help: Upper bound of the histogram range.

parameters.label: Area Weighted
parameters.help: If false, each bin reports the number of vertices in the range. If true, each bin reports the approximate mesh area associated with those values.

parameters.label: Bin Number
parameters.help: The number of bins of the histogram.

filters.name: Measure Face Scalar Histogram
filters.shortDescription: Compute a histogram of per-face quality values.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Compute an histogram of the values of the per-face quality.

parameters.label: Hist Min
parameters.help: Lower bound of the histogram range.

parameters.label: Hist Max
parameters.help: Upper bound of the histogram range.

parameters.label: Area Weighted
parameters.help: If false, each bin reports the number of faces in the range. If true, each bin reports the approximate area in that range.

parameters.label: Bin Number
parameters.help: The number of bins of the histogram.
